cohort: The study included 83 pregnant asthmatic patients aged 18-38 years and a control group of 83 pregnant patients without asthma diagnosis or symptoms.
finding: Respiratory tract infections and adequate asthma treatment are the most important modifiable factors in preventing perinatal complications associated with asthma, with a significantly higher incidence of cesarean section found in asthmatic pregnancies, particularly those with severe or uncontrolled asthma.
mod_finding: The incidence of cesarean section was significantly higher among patients with asthma, especially in those with severe and uncontrolled asthma.
